- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Le Verrier made the prediction based on calculations of the orbit of Uranus, which appeared to be disturbed by the gravitational influence of an unknown planet.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Le Verrier sent his predictions to German astronomer Johann Gottfried Galle, who then used them to discover the new planet, which was named Neptune.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Neptune was first observed on September 23, 1846.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Example 1: Higgs Boson - The Higgs boson is a subatomic particle predicted by the Standard Model of particle physics, proposed by physicist Peter Higgs in 1964, discovered in 2012 at the Large Hadron Collider.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Example 2: General Relativity - Albert Einstein's theory predicted the bending of light by gravity, observed during a solar eclipse in 1919.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Example 3: Plate Tectonics - The theory was first proposed in the 1960s, confirmed decades later by evidence from seismology, paleomagnetism, and other fields.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Example 4: Black Holes - The idea was first proposed by physicist John Michell in the late 18th century, more fully understood and confirmed by observational evidence in the 1960s.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Example 5: DNA Structure - The double helix structure was proposed by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953, confirmed through experimental evidence several years later, involving the work of Rosalind Franklin and others.
